questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">The energy per unit area associated with a progressive sound wave will be doubled if :<\/div>$\n$
options: the amplitude of the wave is doubled
the amplitude of the wave is increased by 50%
the amplitude of the wave is increased by 41%
the frequency of the wave is increased by 41%
questions.explanation:
**Explanation:
$ We$ must determine which changes will double the energy per unit area of a sound wave.
$ $
$ $**Concept:
$ This$ question is based on:
$ Energy$ (Intensity) ∝ A² f²
$ $
$ $**Solution:
$ Intensity$ of a sound wave:
$ I$ ∝ A² f²
$ $
$ To$ double the energy:
$ I \u$2082 = 2 I$\u$2081
$ $
$ Case$ 1: Change in amplitude
$ Let$ amplitude be A$\u$2081 initially and A$\u$2082 finally.
$ $
$ A \u$2082² = 2 A$\u$2081²
$ A \u$2082 = A$\u$2081 √2
$ $
$ Percentage$ increase:
$ [(A₂ − A₁) / A₁]$ × 100
$ $= (√2 − 1) × 100
$ $≈ (1.414 − 1) × 100
$ $≈ 41%
$ $
$ Case$ 2: Change in frequency
$ Let$ frequency be f$\u$2081 initially and f$\u$2082 finally.
$ $
$ f \u$2082² = 2 f$\u$2081²
$ f \u$2082 = f$\u$2081 √2
$ $
$ Percentage$ increase:
$ [(f₂ − f₁) / f₁]$ × 100
$ $= (√2 − 1) × 100
$ $≈ 41%
$ $
$ $**Final Answer: Option (3) & (4)
$ $
